components: Leaderless replication: submits a versioned mutation
Leaderless replication: orders or coordinates writes
Leaderless replication: stores a durable copy
Leaderless replication: selects a freshness level

steps: A coordinator sends v7 directly to all key replicas.
Two acknowledgements satisfy the configured write quorum.
A later reader gathers two replica versions.
The resolver selects a causal descendant or returns concurrent siblings for merge.

lesson.scenario: A coordinator writes a session value directly to three replicas and reconciles divergent versions.

steps.title: Divergent baseline
steps.narration: A and B hold [4,2], while C contains concurrent [3,3].
steps.outcome: No permanent leader owns the key.
steps.invariant: Each version needs metadata sufficient to detect causality or concurrency.

steps.title: Parallel read
steps.narration: The client-side coordinator reads all three replicas.
steps.outcome: The quorum exposes both concurrent siblings.
steps.invariant: A response cannot select a winner solely by arrival order.

steps.title: Sibling detection
steps.outcome: Both application changes must be considered.
steps.invariant: Concurrent versions are retained until a deterministic or application merge resolves them.

steps.title: Application merge
steps.narration: The resolver combines cart and coupon into descendant [4,3].
steps.outcome: The client receives a value preserving both edits.
steps.invariant: The merged version must dominate every resolved sibling.

steps.title: Read repair
steps.narration: The merged descendant is written back to stale replicas.
steps.outcome: The leaderless replicas converge after repair.
steps.invariant: Repair must not erase a version that is newer than the repair payload.
